text:
Samir Naik: hey team, first day — merged onboarding kubeconfig with my personal one and now kubectl shows the company context in terminal but VSCode/kubernetes extension still shows minikube and my requests are being handled as a serviceaccount (I see system:serviceaccount...). Any ideas?

DevEx Bot: welcome Samir! :wave: Quick checklist: 1) run `kubectl config current-context` in both terminal and inside VSCode integrated terminal; 2) check VSCode workspace setting `kubernetes.kubeconfig`; 3) `kubectl config get-contexts -o name` and `kubectl config use-context <name>`; 4) avoid sudo when moving ~/.kube/config (fix ownership with `chown`).

Samir Naik: terminal shows onb-samir@dev, VSCode shows minikube; I found workspace had an override pointing at an old file. changed it and reloaded, now extension matches terminal. But still `kubectl describe pod` gives `forbidden` and I see `system:serviceaccount:onboard-samir:default` in logs.

Jordan L.: that often means the active context is pointing to a different cluster entry with the same name (merge collision). Run `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.clusters[0].cluster.server}'` and verify the server URL. Also `kubectl config view users` to confirm the user is your OIDC user, not a token tied to a SA.

Samir Naik: server is https://dev.internal:6443 and user shows samir.naik@company (oidc). But when I `--kubeconfig=~/downloads/onboard.yaml describe pod` it works as my user. So merged config seems to have a context name pointing to the wrong cluster entry.

Diego R.: rename contexts before merging: `kubectl config rename-context onb@dev onb-samir@dev` and same for minikube. Then `kubectl config view --merge --flatten` and inspect before replacing. If you need immediate access I'll create a short RoleBinding.

Onboarding Bot: Hi Samir — I don't see you in group `eng-onboarding` yet. Creating a 48h RoleBinding for `user:samir.naik@company` -> `Role:onboard-reader` in `onboard-samir` now. Reply here if you need permanent group add.

Samir Naik: rolebinding applied and tests pass, can list and describe pods now. Thanks all! I'll keep company kubeconfigs separate and rename contexts before flattening.
